name: Inbound email triage: classify, draft, approve, reply (IMAP + SMTP)

parameters.content:
## Inbound email triage: classify, draft, approve, reply (IMAP + SMTP)

### How it works

This workflow triages inbound email by polling an IMAP inbox or accepting an optional webhook payload, then normalizes each message into a common structure. It calls AI services to classify the message and draft a reply, then routes the draft through an approval gate. Approved replies are sent via SMTP and logged, while drafts requiring review are queued, logged, and sent to an approver notification channel.

### Setup steps

- Configure IMAP credentials and mailbox settings for fetching unseen email.
- Configure SMTP credentials and sender/reply threading fields for sending responses.
- Set the AI endpoint variables `CLASSIFY_API_URL` and `DRAFT_API_URL`, including any required authentication headers on the HTTP Request nodes.
- Set `DB_WRITE_API_URL` for sent and pending-review logging.
- Set `APPROVAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL` for Slack, email, or another approver notification service.
- If using push mode or approval callbacks, expose and secure the webhook trigger URLs.

### Customization

Adjust the approval gate logic to decide which categories can auto-send, tune the classification and drafting prompts in the AI endpoints, and modify the queue/notification format to match the review process.

## Scheduled email intake

Polls the inbox every five minutes and fetches unseen messages through IMAP before passing them into the main triage pipeline.

## Optional webhook intake

Provides a separate push-based entry point for messages arriving from another system or channel API, spatially separated from the scheduled IMAP path.

## Normalize incoming message

Converts messages from IMAP or webhook input into a consistent internal shape containing subject, sender, thread, and body fields.

## Classify and draft

Sends the normalized email to AI services to classify it as strict JSON and generate a reply draft in the desired tone.

## Approval routing gate

Determines whether human approval is required and branches the workflow toward either immediate sending or the review queue.

## Send and log reply

Handles the approved path by replying in the same email thread via SMTP and writing a sent-reply log entry.

## Queue human review

Creates a pending-review queue item, logs that the draft is awaiting approval, and notifies the approver through the configured Slack or email webhook.

## Approval callback endpoint

Receives approval actions from the review process through a separate webhook entry point located near the human-review area of the canvas.

nodes.name: Poll Every 15 Minutes
nodes.notes: Optional trigger A: drives IMAP polling on a schedule (every 15 min by default). Adjust to hourly or daily depending on inbox volume.

nodes.name: Webhook for Email Inbound
nodes.notes: Optional trigger B: receives JSON messages forwarded from Gmail API / Outlook / a form system. In production use either this or the schedule trigger — never both, or messages are processed twice.

nodes.name: Fetch Unseen Emails
nodes.notes: IMAP inbox. Create the credential in n8n Credentials (host / port / user / password / SSL). You need {{IMAP_HOST}}, {{IMAP_USER}}, {{IMAP_PASSWORD}} (a Gmail app password works).

nodes.name: Normalize Email Message
nodes.notes: Code node. After importing, verify the field names against your mail provider's payload and adjust the mapping.

nodes.name: Classify Email Content
nodes.notes: HTTP Request node. Replace the URL and body placeholders. It sends no auth header by default — if your endpoint needs one, configure Header Auth in n8n and add an Authorization header. {{CLASSIFY_LANGUAGE}} = zh / en / auto.

nodes.name: Draft AI Reply
nodes.notes: HTTP Request node. Replace the URL and body placeholders and add Header Auth if needed. Expected response shape: {"ok":true,"data":{"draft":"...","review_required":false}}.

nodes.name: Determine Approval Requirement
nodes.notes: Code node. After importing, verify the field names and the approval rules (autoSend switch, complaint and low-confidence handling).

nodes.name: If Auto Send Approved
nodes.notes: true branch = send automatically; false branch = wait for human approval. Re-check the IF condition types in the n8n UI so a string "false" is not treated as true.

nodes.name: Send SMTP Reply
nodes.notes: SMTP send. Thread headers (In-Reply-To / References) are set by the node so the reply lands in the customer's existing thread. Swap in an official Gmail/Outlook node if you prefer.

nodes.name: Log Sent Email
nodes.notes: HTTP Request node. Replace the URL and body placeholders; add Header Auth if your logging endpoint requires it.

nodes.name: Queue for Human Approval
nodes.notes: Code node. Marks the draft as pending_review and builds the notification text for the approver.

nodes.name: Notify Approver for Review
nodes.notes: HTTP Request node. Point it at your Slack bot or email endpoint. Delete this node if you don't want notifications.

nodes.name: Log Awaiting Approval
nodes.notes: HTTP Request node. Replace the URL and body placeholders. The real send after approval is wired through the approval webhook (queue_id → fetch draft → SMTP).

nodes.name: Approval Callback Webhook
nodes.notes: Placeholder: called when a human clicks approve. Input {queue_id, decision: approve|reject}. Deliberately left disconnected so importing the template cannot send anything by itself.

notes:
**Template skeleton — read before importing.**
This file is a working skeleton, not a plug-and-play product. After importing:

1) **Mailbox credentials** — create an IMAP credential (emailReadImap) and an SMTP credential in n8n Credentials, then re-select them on the trigger and send nodes (the file references {{IMAP_CREDENTIAL_ID}} / {{SMTP_CREDENTIAL_ID}} placeholders).
2) **Service URLs** — replace {{CLASSIFY_API_URL}}, {{DRAFT_API_URL}}, {{DB_WRITE_API_URL}} and {{APPROVAL_NOTIFY_WEBHOOK_URL}} with your own endpoints (any OpenAI-compatible API works).
3) **Pick ONE trigger** — production should use a single entry point: a) Schedule + IMAP polling, b) IMAP polling only (activate the IMAP node as trigger), or c) Webhook (forwarded from Gmail API / Outlook / other channel). Both the Schedule and Webhook paths are wired into "Normalise message" here — enabling both at once processes the same email twice, so disable the one you don't use.
4) **Human approval switch** — autoSend defaults to false: every draft goes to the review queue first. Change the constant in the "Route: approval required?" node to switch a category to auto-send.
5) **Secrets** — keep API keys in n8n credentials or environment variables, never inside nodes.

To add Gmail/Outlook/other channels, put an adapter in front of the Webhook trigger.
